extracted.intended_audience: organizations preparing sustainability / non‑financial / ESG reports (large or small, private or public), and stakeholders such as investors, policymakers and civil society
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing sustainability (ESG/non‑financial) reports using the GRI Standards system, including Universal, Sector and Topic Standards, and expectations on materiality, due diligence and alignment with other frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report impacts in a comparable and credible way
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI Standards enable any organization – large or small, private or public – to understand and report on their impacts on the economy, environment and people in a comparable and credible way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should increase transparency on an organisation’s contribution to sustainable development by producing comparable, credible disclosures about economic, environmental and social impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular structure: report material topics, impacts and management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standards are designed as an easy-to-use modular set, delivering an inclusive picture of an organization's material topics, their related impacts, and how they are managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the modular system (Universal, Sector, Topic Standards) to identify material topics, describe related impacts, and explain management approaches for those impacts. See 'Get to know the GRI Standards system' for how to apply modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Standards: include human rights and environmental due diligence; apply to all organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal Standards - incorporate reporting on human rights and environmental due diligence, in line with intergovernmental expectations, and apply to all organizations;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reporting organisations must follow the Universal Standards which require disclosure on human rights and environmental due diligence consistent with intergovernmental expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector Standards: consistent sector‑specific impact reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sector Standards enable more consistent reporting on sector-specific impacts;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, use Sector Standards to ensure consistent disclosure of impacts that are specific to an organisation’s industry or sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Standards: list disclosures relevant to a particular topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic Standards - list disclosures relevant to a particular topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and apply Topic Standards to report on specific areas (e.g., climate, biodiversity, labor) and follow the listed disclosures for those topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous improvement: regular review to reflect global best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRI Standards are regularly reviewed to ensure they reflect global best practices for sustainability reporting, helping thousands of organizations around the world respond to emerging information demands from stakeholders and regulators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect periodic updates and consultations; reporting should adapt to reflect updated Standards and evolving stakeholder/regulatory information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards interpretations: clarifications on reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards interpretations — Issued clarifications on reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult official interpretations for clarifications where reporting requirements are ambiguous; interpretations explain how to apply requirements in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global alignment: link Standards to other frameworks and initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Global alignment — How the Standards link to other frameworks and initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GRI guidance and mappings (e.g., GRI‑CDP alignment) to connect GRI disclosures with other reporting frameworks and questionnaires to improve decision‑usefulness and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and translations: Standards available to download and in multiple languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Download the Standards — Translations of the Standards are available in many languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and supporting documents are freely accessible and translated; organisations should use available translations and materials to support clear, accessible reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timing: comply with effective dates of revised Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised Universal Standards were published in October 2021 and came into effect for reporting on 1 January 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must follow the version of the Standards that is in effect for the reporting period; be aware of revision publication dates and effective dates when preparing reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register published sustainability reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Register your report — Register your published sustainability report here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication, organisations are encouraged (or required by the system) to register their sustainability/GRI reports in the GRI registry to increase transparency and discoverability.
